question.value: Characterize the 1.3 mm continuum (thermal dust vs non-thermal synchrotron) and serendipitous molecular gas line properties of high-redshift radio galaxy (HzRG) candidates selected in the ELAIS-S1 field, and evaluate the efficiency of IR-radio selection criteria.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure 1.3 mm continuum fluxes and stack undetected sources

method.value: Fit elliptical Gaussian components to detections > 4.2 sigma and detections > 3 sigma matching an IRAC source using CASA imfit; stack continuum maps of 11 undetected sources at z > 0.8.

evidence.quote: Using the imfit task from casa, which fits elliptical Gaussian components to specified regions, we retrieved the fluxes for all detections above $4.2\sigma$ as well as for detections above $3\sigma$ matching with a known IRAC source

In order to assess the flux of the undetected sources in the sample, we have pursued a stacking analysis considering only those sources at $z>0.8$ and devoid of $>3\sigma$ signal in the central region.

The ‘b’ suffix indicates sources in the ACA FoV detected at or above 3$\sigma$ further away than 3.5$''$ from the radio source (and therefore not associated to it), but co-located with an IRAC detection above 3$\sigma$ to within 2$''$.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit radio SEDs and extrapolate synchrotron contribution at 233 GHz

method.value: Match candidates with GLEAM (65'' radius) and TGSS (15'' radius); fit multi-frequency radio photometry (150 MHz to 2.3 GHz) with a single power law S_nu propto nu^alpha and extrapolate to 233 GHz to classify mm emission as synchrotron or thermal.

evidence.quote: For this we adopted 65$''$ and 15$''$ matching radii with GLEAM and TGSS, respectively, equivalent to a 1$\sigma$ matching region
We fit the radio SEDs with a power law with a single spectral index ($S_\nu\propto\nu^\alpha$), indicated by the dotted line.

The extrapolation of the SED fit to the reference frequency of our ACA observations at 233\,GHz, assuming the same single power law, allows for an estimate of the flux due to synchrotron emission at that frequency.

key_parameters.value: GLEAM 200 MHz-wide band (170-231 MHz); N = 100 bootstrap iterations; synchrotron-dominated threshold S^fit_233 > 0.5 * S^obs_233 within 1 sigma; thermal-dominated threshold S^fit_233 < 0.5 * S^obs_233 by > 3 sigma

evidence.quote: The latter was pursued by refitting the radio SED after randomly drawing new flux values (N$=$100) assuming a normal distribution characterised by the flux uncertainty around the mean value.

This is the case when the predicted flux at 233 GHz, S$^{fit}_{233}$, is greater than 50% of the observed flux within 1 $\sigma$. On the other hand, if S$^{fit}_{233}$ falls below 50% of the observed flux by more than 3 $\sigma$, we consider that thermal emission dominates at these frequencies

assumptions.value: Single power law S_nu propto nu^alpha from radio to 233 GHz; for sources with <= 2 radio points, assumed median spectral index alpha = -0.68 with population deviation factor of 1.4.

evidence.quote: The spectral index, $\alpha$, reported in the fourth column in parenthesis indicates the availability of up to two radio data points only. In such cases, a value of $-0.68$ was adopted with population deviation factor of 1.4 (Fig. [8](#fig:radiosedrf)).

analysis_steps.goal: Derive molecular gas masses from dust continuum and CO(5-4) line luminosities

method.value: Convert synchrotron-corrected 1.3 mm continuum fluxes to M_H2 using the Scoville et al. (2016) relation; convert CO(5-4) line luminosities of sources 20 and 32 to M_H2 using assumed CO excitation ratios and alpha_CO.

claims.hypothesis: Simple MIR colour cuts combined with radio flux or spectral criteria can efficiently select high-redshift radio galaxies (z > 0.8).
claims.experiment: Applied USS, LRS, and IFRS selection criteria using Spitzer SEIP MIR and multi-frequency radio catalogues in ELAIS-S1, and evaluated the resulting redshift distributions.
claims.result: 77% of the sample with redshifts lie at z > 0.8 (median z = 1.4), with the LRS criterion achieving an 86% selection rate at z > 0.8 (4 out of 29 at z < 0.8).
claims.finding: The LRS criterion (S_5.8/S_3.6 > 1.3 and S_1.4GHz > 1 mJy) provides the highest reliability and largest candidate yield, though shallow 5.8 um data biases the sample toward z ~ 1.4 and luminous sources.

evidence.quote: The criterion providing the highest selection rate of high-redshift sources (86% at $z>0.8$) is one combining an IR colour cut and radio flux cut ($S_{\rm 5.8\mu m} / S_{\rm 3.6\mu m}>1.3$ and $S_{\rm 1.4\,GHz}>1\,$mJy).
Overall, the LRS criterion is the least contaminated by $z<0.8$ objects in fractional terms (4 out of 29 sources or 14% versus 20% and 25% for IFRS and USS samples, respectively).

claims.hypothesis: 1.3 mm continuum observations of HzRGs trace thermal cold dust emission from star formation in the host galaxies.
claims.experiment: Observed 36 HzRG candidates with ACA Band 6 (233 GHz) to rms ~ 0.15 mJy and extrapolated low-frequency (150 MHz - 2.3 GHz) power-law radio SEDs to 233 GHz.
claims.result: 16 of 36 central sources are detected at 1.3 mm, but in 8 of the 16 detections the extrapolated synchrotron flux accounts for >50% of the 233 GHz emission; in source 32, the 1.3 mm continuum is offset by 1.5 +- 0.8'' from the host CO(5-4) gas.
claims.finding: At z < 2, non-thermal synchrotron emission from the AGN/jet frequently dominates at 1.3 mm in luminous radio galaxies, preventing direct study of host thermal dust emission in half of the detected sample.

evidence.quote: Out of the 16 central detections, 8 are of non-thermal origin (Sec. [2.2](#sec:radphot), Tab. [3](#tab:radiosed)), leaving only 8 where ACA is detecting the dust emission from the host galaxy.
We finally caution against the use of the mm spectral range to study the host galaxies of the most luminous radio-galaxies at least at $z<2$ (where most of our sample lies).

claims.hypothesis: Significant (> 4 sigma) negative continuum decrements around four observed radio galaxies are caused by the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect (kSZE) from AGN-driven gas outflows.
claims.experiment: Performed uv-space source subtraction, visibility fitting (uv-multifit), N=2000 visibility bootstrap simulations, ACT CMB map checks, and analytical kSZE modelling for source ap5.
claims.result: Simulations show at least one negative peak (ap5, S_233 ~ -1 mJy) is unlikely to be spurious, and ACT maps rule out cluster-scale tSZE; however, reproducing a -1 mJy kSZE decrement requires M_gas ~ 10^11 - 10^13 M_sun or v ~ 0.26c.
claims.finding: While at least one decrement appears statistically robust against calibration artefacts, a pure kSZE origin requires implausibly extreme gas masses or relativistic velocities, necessitating multi-frequency follow-up.

evidence.quote: Purely based on location while comparing with the simulations results (Fig. [12](#fig:sims)) it is shown that at least one source should be considered as highly reliable.

why_this_data.value: ELAIS-S1 has low foreground contamination, deep multi-wavelength (X-ray to radio) coverage, and fits the under-subscribed LST range required for an ACA Observatory Filler Programme; sensitivity (0.2 mJy requested) was chosen to match SCUBA2 850 um depth (~1.2 mJy).

evidence.loc: The choice of the ELAIS-S1 field
evidence.quote: As OFPs are meant to fill the ACA observing queue in under-subscribed Local Sidereal Time (LST) ranges, the targets had to be selected in a field in the adequate RA range with, at the same time, available multi-wavelength ancillary data.

The requested sensitivity of 0.2\,mJy was set to match that of $\sim$1.2\,mJy at 850\,$\mu$m provided by SCUBA2 maps (cite: geach17) assuming a thermal-like spectral slope of $\alpha=3.9$ (with $S_\nu\propto\nu^\alpha$).

(2015) because M08 covers the full radio area and groups multi-lobe radio sources; used Briggs robust = 1.5 instead of 0.5 to improve rms from ~0.23 mJy to ~0.15 mJy; used SoFiA on multi-resolution cubes with inverted-cube validation for unbiased line finding.

evidence.quote: Given the consistency between the two catalogues, we chose not to use F15 as their analysis does not consider the full radio-coverage and does not group multiple radio lobes into single sources, as it is done in M08
The achieved sensitivity reached $\sim$0.15\,mJy by imaging with a Briggs weighting and a robust parameter of 1.5 (a robust parameter of 0.5 would have resulted in an rms$\sim$0.23\,mJy).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rejected using the deeper Franzen et al. (2015) or flux-deboosted Hales et al. (2014) 1.4 GHz catalogues in favour of Middelberg et al. (2008) because F15 covers a smaller area and does not group radio lobes.

evidence.quote: Given the consistency between the two catalogues, we chose not to use F15 as their analysis does not consider the full radio-coverage and does not group multiple radio lobes into single sources, as it is done in M08, increasing the possibility for erroneous cross-matchings.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rejected Briggs robust = 0.5 weighting in favour of robust = 1.5 because robust = 0.5 yielded a higher rms (~0.23 mJy vs ~0.15 mJy).

evidence.quote: The achieved sensitivity reached $\sim$0.15\,mJy by imaging with a Briggs weighting and a robust parameter of 1.5 (a robust parameter of 0.5 would have resulted in an rms$\sim$0.23\,mJy).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Discarded large-scale cluster thermal or kinetic SZE as the origin of the negative continuum peaks because ACT CMB maps show no large-scale tSZE imprints toward the four sources.

evidence.loc: The Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effect as a physical explanation
evidence.quote: We have checked in Atacama Cosmology Telescope (cite: Naess2020; Hilton2021) maps for evidence of large scale tSZE imprints on the CMB. However, we find no significant features toward the four mentioned galaxies. As a result, we discard the possibility that these features are due to bulk motion of the inter-cluster gas

how_they_decided_enough.value: Used N=2000 visibility bootstrap simulations and counts of negative 3-4.2 sigma features to establish that > 4.2 sigma continuum detections are reliable and that 3-4.2 sigma detections are reliable when matched within 2'' of an IRAC source; required positive line candidates in SoFiA to exceed the most significant negative feature across all inverted cubes.

evidence.quote: We also note that we find 27 negative features with significances between $3\sigma$ and $4.2\sigma$. None of them matches in position with an IRAC source. This implies that of order 27 of the positive detections in this signal-to-noise range would be expected to be spurious, consistent with the 26 we discard.

The reported lines are those which, in a given spectral smoothing, showed a velocity integrated signal more significant than any of the negative spurious ones identified among all the inverted cubes at a given spectral smoothing.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-power-law extrapolation over two orders of magnitude in frequency (from ~1 GHz to 233 GHz) ignores potential spectral ageing, steepening, or high-frequency turnovers in radio AGN lobes/cores, which could lead to overestimating the synchrotron contribution at 233 GHz.
For 10 sources lacking >2 radio bands, a fixed median spectral index of alpha = -0.68 is assumed to extrapolate to 233 GHz, introducing substantial classification uncertainty.

All four >4 sigma negative continuum features fall in the north-east quadrant relative to the phase centre, which strongly suggests a residual phase/amplitude calibration or uv-coverage artefact despite the bootstrap tests.
Molecular gas masses derived from CO(5-4) rely on highly uncertain CO(5-4)/CO(1-0) excitation ratios (0.3-0.7) and alpha_CO (0.5-1.0), spanning nearly an order of magnitude in systematic uncertainty.
